name: China Permanent Residence (Chinese Green Card) — Complete 2026 Guide
description: Everything about China's Permanent Residence permit (Chinese Green Card): eligibility pathways, application requirements, provincial variation, and benefits. China's permanent residence permit, informally known as the Chinese Green Card, grants indefinite residence and work authorization in China. Published guidelines indicate multiple pathways to permanent residence: long-term employment on a Z Visa (typically 4+ years of continuous employment with 3+ years of cumulative residence), high-level talent certification on an R Visa (preferred and faster pathway), significant investment or business contributions, and marriage to a Chinese citizen. Requirements vary by province, with tier-1 cities like Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen having more established programs. Permanent residence holders enjoy unrestricted work authorization, simplified re-entry, and rights comparable to Chinese citizens in many respects excluding voting and public office. The application process involves the local Public Security Bureau and typically takes 6-12 months. Updated for 2026.
tagline: Indefinite residence and unrestricted work authorization in China
keyRequirement: Long-term continuous employment (4+ years) or high-level talent certification or significant investment
targetAudience: Long-term Z Visa holders with 4+ years of continuous employment in China
R Visa holders with government talent certification seeking permanent status
Foreign investors with significant and stable investments in China
Foreign spouses of Chinese citizens with 5+ years of marriage
Senior professionals who have made substantial contributions to China's economic or social development

eligibility.label: Continuous employment for 4+ years on a work visa with 3+ years cumulative residence
eligibility.description: Published guidelines indicate that Z Visa holders with continuous employment for at least 4 years, cumulative residence in China of at least 3 years during that period, and stable income and tax contributions may apply. The specific income threshold varies by province.

eligibility.label: R Visa holders with government talent certification (preferred pathway)
eligibility.description: High-level talent certified by authorized government agencies (Organization Department of CPC Central Committee, MOHRSS, or State Administration of Foreign Experts Affairs) have a preferred and expedited pathway to permanent residence. Published guidelines indicate shorter residency requirements for this category.

eligibility.label: Significant and stable investment in China for 3+ years
eligibility.description: Foreign investors with stable and substantial investment in China for at least 3 years may apply. The investment amount threshold varies by province and city, with higher thresholds in tier-1 cities. Investment must demonstrate contribution to economic development.

eligibility.label: Married to a Chinese citizen with 5+ years of marriage and 5+ years of continuous residence
eligibility.description: Foreign spouses of Chinese citizens who have been married for at least 5 years and have resided continuously in China for at least 5 years may apply. Must demonstrate stable living conditions and income.

eligibility.label: No criminal record, good health, and compliance with Chinese laws
eligibility.description: All applicants regardless of pathway must have no criminal record in China or their home country, be in good health, and have a history of compliance with Chinese immigration and tax laws.

duration.extension: Permanent residence card must be renewed every 10 years (status itself is indefinite)
duration.maxTotal: No limit — permanent residence status does not expire

fees.notes: Additional costs for document legalization, translations, and medical examinations apply. Fees are subject to change — verify with the local Public Security Bureau before applying.

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Current valid passport with all previous Chinese visa pages. Previous passports with China visa history may also be requested.

documents.name: Permanent Residence Application Form
documents.nameLocal: 外国人永久居留申请表
documents.description: Official application form obtained from the local Entry-Exit Administration of the Public Security Bureau. Must be completed in Chinese or with Chinese translations.

documents.name: Passport-Sized Photos
documents.description: Recent photos (within 6 months), white background, full face, no hat. Multiple copies may be required (typically 4-6).

documents.name: Medical Examination Certificate
documents.description: Health examination certificate from a designated medical institution in China. Must be recent (within 6 months of application).

documents.name: Criminal Background Check
documents.description: Criminal background check from China (issued by local PSB) and from your home country (legalized through the standard chain: notarize, apostille, Chinese embassy legalization). Both are typically required.
tips: The Chinese criminal background check can be obtained from the local Public Security Bureau
The home country background check must be legalized — not just apostilled

documents.name: Continuous Employment Records
documents.description: Employment contracts, work permits, and employer certificates covering the entire qualifying employment period. Must demonstrate continuous employment without gaps.
tips: Organize records chronologically to demonstrate continuous employment
Include all work permit renewals and employer changes

documents.name: Tax Payment Certificates
documents.description: Individual income tax payment records for the qualifying period, issued by the local tax authority. Must demonstrate consistent tax contributions throughout the residence period.
tips: Request tax certificates from the local tax bureau
Higher tax contributions strengthen the application

documents.name: Residence Registration Records
documents.description: PSB registration records and residence permit history demonstrating continuous residence in China for the qualifying period.

documents.name: Proof of Stable Housing
documents.description: Property ownership certificate, long-term lease agreement, or other proof of stable housing arrangement in China.

documents.name: Talent Certification Documents (R Visa pathway)
documents.description: Confirmation Letter for High Level Foreign Talents and supporting credential documentation. Required for the talent pathway; not needed for other pathways.

applicationSteps.title: Determine Eligibility Pathway
applicationSteps.description: Assess which permanent residence pathway applies to your situation: long-term employment, talent certification, investment, or marriage. Each pathway has different documentation requirements and qualifying periods. Published guidelines vary by province.
tips: The talent pathway (R Visa) is generally the fastest and most straightforward
Consult with the local Entry-Exit Administration for province-specific requirements before gathering documents

applicationSteps.title: Gather All Required Documents
applicationSteps.description: Compile the full documentation package for your chosen pathway: employment records, tax certificates, residence history, medical examination, criminal background checks (both Chinese and home country), housing proof, and pathway-specific documents.
tips: The home country criminal background check with Chinese embassy legalization takes the longest — start this first
Request tax certificates and employment verification letters from current and previous employers in advance

applicationSteps.title: Submit Application at Entry-Exit Administration
applicationSteps.description: Submit the complete application at the Entry-Exit Administration of the Public Security Bureau in your city of residence. An officer will review the documents and may ask for additional materials.
tips: Bring all original documents plus copies
Some cities allow appointment booking — check with your local office
Have a Chinese-speaking person accompany you if your Chinese is limited

applicationSteps.title: Application Review and Investigation
applicationSteps.description: The Public Security Bureau reviews your application, verifies documents, and may conduct background investigations. They may request additional documentation or schedule an interview during this period.
tips: Respond to any requests for additional documents promptly
The review process is generally faster in tier-1 cities with more established programs

applicationSteps.title: Receive Decision and Permanent Residence Card
applicationSteps.description: Upon approval, you will be notified to collect your permanent residence card (Chinese Green Card) at the Entry-Exit Administration. The card serves as your identification document and proof of permanent residence status.
applicationSteps.duration: 2-4 weeks for card production after approval
tips: The permanent residence card must be renewed every 10 years, but the status itself is indefinite
Your passport will also receive a permanent residence stamp

processingTime.notes: Processing times vary significantly by province and application pathway. Tier-1 cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou) generally have more established processes but also higher application volumes. The talent pathway (R Visa holders) may receive expedited processing. Published guidelines indicate total review time should not exceed 6 months, but practical timelines are often longer.

workPermission.notes: Permanent residence holders have unrestricted work authorization in China. This includes changing employers freely, starting a business, and holding multiple positions. No separate work permit is required. Work authorization is not tied to any specific employer or location.

faqs.question: What are the main pathways to Chinese permanent residence?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate four main pathways: (1) Long-term employment — 4+ years continuous employment on a work visa with 3+ years cumulative residence; (2) High-level talent — R Visa holders with government talent certification, which offers a preferred and shorter timeline; (3) Investment — significant and stable investment in China for 3+ years; (4) Marriage — married to a Chinese citizen for 5+ years with 5+ years of continuous residence. Each pathway has specific documentation and qualifying requirements that vary by province.

faqs.question: How does provincial variation affect the application?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate that permanent residence requirements vary significantly by province and city. Tier-1 cities (Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou) have more established talent programs and clearer documentation requirements, but also higher income thresholds. Smaller cities may have different investment thresholds or employment duration requirements. It is advisable to consult with the local Entry-Exit Administration in your city of residence for specific requirements.

faqs.question: Is the Chinese Green Card the same as citizenship?
faqs.answer: No. The Chinese Green Card (permanent residence permit) grants the right to reside and work in China indefinitely, but it is not citizenship. Permanent residents cannot vote, hold public office, or obtain a Chinese passport. China does not formally recognize dual citizenship — obtaining Chinese citizenship would require renouncing your current nationality. The permanent residence permit provides most practical rights of citizenship for daily life and work.

faqs.question: Can my family also receive permanent residence?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate that family members (spouse and minor children) of permanent residence holders may apply for permanent residence through the family pathway. The requirements for family members are generally less stringent than for the primary applicant. Spouses typically need to demonstrate stable marriage and continuous residence. Minor children may be included in the family application.

faqs.question: What happens if I leave China for an extended period?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate that permanent residence holders must reside in China for a cumulative minimum period within each validity cycle of the card (typically 3 months per year or 1 year per 5 years, though specific requirements vary). Extended absence from China without maintaining minimum residence may result in the permanent residence status being reviewed or revoked. Consult the local Entry-Exit Administration for specific continuous residence requirements.

faqs.question: How often must the permanent residence card be renewed?
faqs.answer: The permanent residence card must be renewed every 10 years, similar to a passport renewal. However, the permanent residence status itself is indefinite — card renewal is an administrative procedure, not a re-evaluation of eligibility. Apply for card renewal before the expiration date at the Entry-Exit Administration. The renewal fee is approximately 300 RMB.

faqs.question: Which pathway is fastest for permanent residence?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate that the R Visa (talent) pathway is generally considered the fastest route to permanent residence. High-level talent with government certification may have shorter residency requirements and more streamlined processing compared to the standard employment pathway, which requires a minimum of 4 years of continuous employment. The specific timeline varies by province and individual circumstances.

faqs.question: Do I need to speak Chinese to apply for permanent residence?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines do not specify a formal Chinese language requirement for permanent residence applications. However, the application process is conducted primarily in Chinese, and forms must be completed in Chinese. Having Chinese language ability or assistance from a Chinese-speaking person is practically important for navigating the process. Some provinces may consider Chinese proficiency as a positive factor in evaluating applications.

faqs.question: What income threshold is required for the employment pathway?
faqs.answer: The specific income threshold for the employment pathway varies by province and is not uniformly published in English-language government sources. Published guidelines indicate that applicants must demonstrate 'stable income and tax contributions' throughout the qualifying period. In tier-1 cities, the practical threshold is generally higher than in other regions. Consistent tax payment records are more important than a specific salary level.

faqs.question: Can I own property in China with permanent residence?
faqs.answer: Published guidelines indicate that permanent residence holders have the right to purchase property in China under the same conditions as Chinese citizens, which is a significant advantage over temporary visa holders who face restrictions on property purchases. This includes both residential and commercial property. Property purchases must comply with local real estate regulations.

tips: Consult with the local Entry-Exit Administration in your city BEFORE gathering documents — requirements vary significantly by province
The R Visa (talent) pathway offers the fastest route — if you have Category A qualifications, consider upgrading from Z to R Visa first
Maintain meticulous records of employment, tax payments, and PSB registrations throughout your stay — these are the backbone of the application
Start the home country criminal background check early — with legalization, this can take 3-6 months
Keep tax payment records organized by year — consistent tax contributions demonstrate economic integration
Build relationships with local immigration officers and consult them periodically about documentation requirements
Engage a qualified immigration consultant or lawyer familiar with your province's specific requirements
Apply before your current residence permit expires to maintain continuous legal status during processing
warnings: Requirements vary significantly by province — do not assume that guidelines from one city apply to another
Gaps in employment, tax payments, or PSB registration records can weaken or disqualify an application
Extended absence from China may jeopardize permanent residence status — maintain minimum residence requirements
The permanent residence card must be renewed every 10 years — failure to renew may cause administrative complications
English-language official documentation of specific requirements is limited — provincial authorities have significant discretion

communityTips.tip: Shanghai has one of the most established and transparent permanent residence programs in China. Published guidelines for Shanghai are clearer and the Entry-Exit Administration staff are more experienced with foreign applicants. If you have flexibility in where you are based, Shanghai may offer a smoother application process.

Tax payment certificates are among the most scrutinized documents in the permanent residence application. Make sure your employer has been correctly withholding and reporting your individual income tax every month throughout your entire employment period. Any gaps or inconsistencies in tax records are difficult to explain.

Engaging a Chinese immigration lawyer or consultant who specializes in permanent residence applications is highly recommended. They know the specific requirements of your local Entry-Exit Administration and can help prepare the documentation package to meet local standards, which vary significantly from the general published guidelines.

If you are on a Z Visa and considering permanent residence, evaluate whether you can first upgrade to an R Visa. The R Visa talent pathway to permanent residence is significantly shorter and more favorable. The investment in obtaining talent certification may pay off through a faster and more certain path to permanent status.

Keep detailed travel records showing your entries and exits from China. The cumulative residence requirement means you need to demonstrate that you have physically been in China for the required number of days. Flight itineraries, passport stamps, and PSB registration records all serve as evidence.

pathsTo.name: Work Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Continuous employment on Z Visa for 4+ years with cumulative residence in China of 3+ years. Stable income, consistent tax contributions, and clean compliance record. Requirements vary by province.
pathsTo.timeline: 4-8 years from initial Z Visa (varies by province and individual circumstances)
documents: Tax payment certificates for the qualifying period
PSB registration and residence permit history
Criminal background checks (Chinese and home country)
pathsTo.notes: The employment pathway is the most common route but has the longest timeline. High-salary earners and those in economically important regions may have shorter effective timelines. Consistent tax contributions and uninterrupted employment records are critical for approval.

pathsTo.name: High-Level Talent Visa
pathsTo.requirements: R Visa with government talent certification. Published guidelines indicate a preferred and faster pathway compared to the standard employment route. Shorter residency requirements apply.
pathsTo.timeline: Shorter than employment pathway (estimated 2-5 years from R Visa, varies by province)
documents: Medical examination and criminal background checks
pathsTo.notes: The talent pathway is widely considered the most favorable route to permanent residence for foreign professionals. Government talent recognition carries significant weight in the application review. Provincial authorities generally process talent pathway applications faster than standard employment applications.
